record.title: Changes in morphological and biochemical blood parameters in dogs with babesiosis
record.journal: Науковий вісник Львівського національного університету ветеринарної медицини та біотехнологій імені С.З. Ґжицького
record.abstract: Babesiosis is one of the most common tick-borne parasitic diseases caused by hemotropic protozoa of the genus Babesia, and is among the leading causes of anemia in dogs. The study was conducted on 10 dogs with a confirmed diagnosis of babesiosis that were treated at the “Aibolit” veterinary clinic in Poltava from March to September 2025. Ten additional animals were randomly selected as a control group. Morphological and biochemical blood parameters were analyzed. The results revealed a 49.2 % decrease in erythrocyte count (P < 0.001), indicating the development of anemia. Hemoglobin levels significantly decreased in diseased dogs by 47.3% (P<0.001). Platelet count dropped to 43.6 ± 11.4 G/L (P < 0.001), while hematocrit levels decreased to 14.2 ± 2.4% (P < 0.001). An increase in monocyte content was also observed in the experimental group, reaching 18.2±2.6% (P<0.01). In the serum of dogs infected with Babesia spp., a significant reduction in total protein by 23.5 % (P < 0.01) and globulin concentrations to 28.4 ± 3.9 g/L (P < 0.05) was detected. The study results also indicate a marked increase in urea, creatinine, total bilirubin, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and alkaline phosphatase activity. Specifically, urea levels increased by 80.1 % (P < 0.001), creatinine by 52.8 % (P < 0.01), AST by 42.4 % (P < 0.001), total bilirubin by 93.2 % (P < 0.001), and alkaline phosphatase by 66.5 % (P < 0.01). A slight elevation of total calcium to 2.4 ± 0.1 mmol/L (P < 0.01) and a decrease in sodium to 130.7 ± 1.9 mmol/L (P < 0.01) were also observed in the serum of affected animals. Thus, the obtained results demonstrate that babesiosis is accompanied by pronounced anemia, thrombocytopenia, and moderate monocytosis, reflecting the systemic response of the organism to parasitic invasion and disruptions of hematopoiesis. Changes in the biochemical blood profile of infected dogs reflect systemic metabolic disturbances, intoxication syndrome, and dysfunction of vital organs, particularly the liver and kidneys, confirming the multiorgan nature of lesions in babesiosis.

screening.rationale: Case-control haematology and biochemistry showing anaemia, thrombocytopenia, renal and hepatic dysfunction, electrolyte changes; multiorgan.
